entities.summary: Usama ibn Zayd ibn Haritha al-Kalbi was a pivotal figure in early Islamic history, born in Mecca, Arabia, around 645 CE, and died in Medina, Arabia, in 678 CE. He was a close companion of the Islamic prophet Muhammad and played a crucial role in the early Muslim community. Usama ibn Zayd was a skilled warrior and military leader, who fought alongside the Prophet Muhammad in several key battles, including the Battle of Tabuk in 630 CE. He was also a trusted advisor and messenger of the Prophet, serving as one of his emissaries during the Ghazwahs (conquests) of Arabia. Usama ibn Zayd's significance lies in his role as a bridge between the pre-Islamic and early Islamic periods, and his contributions to the development of Islamic jurisprudence and governance. His legacy can be seen in the many Islamic scholars and leaders who followed in his footsteps, and his name continues to be revered in many parts of the Muslim world.
